paper_metadata.title: Research on Financial Stock Market Prediction Based on the Hidden Quantum Markov Model

summary: The paper studies hidden quantum Markov model (HQMM) stock forecasting on 15 SSE/SZSE stocks using daily OHLCV data from 1 June 2018 to 23 June 2021. The best reported result is HQMM with GMM+MVTF discretization, achieving average capital of 1,404,827 CNY and average comparative growth rate of 4.96% in 12 min, compared with classical HMM at 1,390,860 CNY, 3.73%, and 40 min.

experiments.description: Hidden quantum Markov model (HQMM) stock trend forecasting on 15 SSE/SZSE stocks, comparing HQMM with evenly discretized data, HQMM with GMM+MVTF discretization, and classical HMM baseline; the quantum experiment is the HQMM model trained via Kraus operators using Qiskit.

algorithm.variant: hidden quantum Markov model (HQMM) with Kraus-operator training
algorithm.convergence_criteria: DA converges / training completed after iterations exceed 40
algorithm.parameter_initialization: ρ0 manually set; Kraus operators initialized from prior configurations and optimized by gradient descent

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Discrete stock trend states S are encoded as observation states for HQMM; six trend states are used after discretization (values 1–6).
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize log-likelihood ς = ln tr(K_Sn ··· (K_S1 ρ0 K†_S1) ··· K†_Sn) under Kraus-operator constraints ∑ K†_m K_m = I, then predict next stock trend state P(S_t|ρ_{t+1}).
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Kraus operators constrained by ∑ K†_m K_m = I; optimization transformed to Stiefel-manifold constrained problem

problem_instance.description: Stock market trend prediction for 15 Chinese stocks from Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges using daily OHLCV data.
problem_instance.dataset_name: SSE/SZSE stock data via Tushare API

dataset_specification.preprocessing: daily opening price, highest price, lowest price, closing price, and trading volume collected; continuous data discretized either by even binning or by GMM+MVTF; 30-day windows used for GMM
dataset_specification.train_test_split: training: 1 June 2018–26 October 2019; validation: 30 October 2019–24 August 2020; testing: 24 August 2020–23 June 2021

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Collect daily OHLCV data; compute day-to-day closing-price differences; split into 30-day groups; fit one-dimensional GMM (n=5 components, K empirically set to 6 in one description); extract means and variances; convert via MVTF into discrete stock trend states; alternative even discretization into six integer states.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compare HQMM and HMM over 15 stocks and three prediction horizons; report average capital, comparative growth rate R, and DA convergence; results summarized across stocks and periods.

implementation_details.classical_solver: hmmlearn / scikit-learn for classical baselines; gradient descent for HQMM training
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: pandas and NumPy preprocessing; GMM and MVTF discretization; even discretization baseline
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute DA, final capital FC, natural capital NC, and comparative growth rate R
implementation_details.total_execution_time: 12 min for HQMM variants; 40 min for HMM baseline

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: DA increases rapidly in first few iterations and converges after about 40 iterations

speedup_claims.conditions: for prediction sequence length T, hidden states n, and observable space dimension w
speedup_claims.caveats: This is an asymptotic complexity comparison; it does not by itself prove wall-clock speedup on all instances.

speedup_claims.conditions: reported total time required: 12 min for HQMM variants vs 40 min for HMM
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports the same 12 min for both HQMM variants; this is a wall-clock comparison on the reported experiments.

speedup_claims.conditions: reported in the paper's summary comparison of total time required
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states 70% faster; this corresponds approximately to 12 min vs 40 min.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: A real gate-based implementation with explicit circuit depth, qubit count, and hardware noise characterization would be needed; the paper only reports a 2x2 Kraus-operator formalism and Qiskit usage, not a deployed QPU experiment.
limiting_factors: No specific quantum hardware or QPU execution is reported
No circuit depth, gate counts, or shot counts are provided
The paper's advantage is based on a model-level comparison, not a hardware-level quantum advantage demonstration
The reported improvement is against a classical HMM baseline and an HQMM discretization variant, not a clear practical quantum advantage on meaningful hardware scale
Data preprocessing/discretization is a major bottleneck for continuous financial time series

notes: hardware.type is not specified in the paper; Qiskit is mentioned, but no QPU or simulator is named, so hardware remains not_specified.
num_qubits inferred as 2 because the paper states each Kraus operator matrix is 2×2 and the density matrix ρ0 is 2×2; the circuit/register size is not explicitly reported.
circuit depth is not explicitly reported; only the number of hidden states and iterations are given.

speedup order inferred as polynomial_other because the paper reports O(Tnw) vs O(Tn2), i.e., a polynomial improvement in the observation-space dimension, not an asymptotic exponential/quadratic speedup claim.

The paper claims better average capital and faster runtime for HQMM with MVTF discretization (1,404,827 CNY, 4.96%, 12 min) versus classical HMM (1,390,860 CNY, 3.73%, 40 min), but no hardware-level quantum advantage is demonstrated.
Because the paper does not report a QPU, the assessment is limited to a theoretical/noiseless-simulation style HQMM formulation.
